abstract: Single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) plays an increasingly important role in structure-based drug discovery (SBDD) by revealing target protein-ligand interactions at the molecular level, but its application has largely focused on large- and medium-sized protein complexes. Many therapeutically important targets are smaller than 50 kDa and remain highly challenging for cryo-EM analysis because of low signal-to-noise ratios and difficulties in particle alignment. Here, we describe cryoFAST, an integrated workflow that couples ligand-compatible Fab discovery and structure-guided computational maturation with biochemical triage, fiducial-complex assembly, and single-particle cryo-EM. Through phage-display screening and/or AI-guided design, we developed high-affinity Fab binders of approximately 50 kDa that stabilize the target without disrupting ligand-target interactions and then assembled Fab-target complexes for cryo-EM analysis. Using the therapeutically relevant extracellular domain (~20 kDa) of interleukin-4 receptor  (IL-4R) as a proof of concept, we determined its cryo-EM structure at 2.74 Angstrom resolution and established a framework for elucidating ligand-binding modes. This workflow provides a practical, efficient, and potentially broadly applicable route to the structural characterization of small protein targets that are otherwise challenging to study. By extending the applicability of cryo-EM to high-value but technically challenging small targets, cryoFAST may open new opportunities for structure-based drug discovery.
